newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 3.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- David Ervine, the Progressive Unionist leader, has cast further gloom over the peace process by declaring his belief that the process would collapse into full scale violence within the next two weeks.
- The Irish government's finances are in the black for the first time in 30 years with a surplus of 185 million Irish pounds for the first nine months of the year.
- Interest rates may fall by as much as one per cent by the end of the year, and Irish taxpayers could enjoy substantial tax cuts in January's budget.

- The Irish government would have to give "serious consideration" to participation in a new international military force in former Yugoslavia which is almost certain to be under NATO command, according to the Deputy Irish Prime Minister, Dick Spring.

- Solicitors for Brigid Ellen McCole, the woman who died on Wednesday after being infected with the hepatitis C virus, reached a compensation settlement with the Blood Transfusion Service Board shortly before her death.

- The Provisional IRA has stockpiled weapons and explosives in a network of hiding places close to the border between the Republic and Northern Ireland in preparation for a major terror campaign directed by hardliners.

- A 54-year old mother of 12 who died from liver failure due to Hepatitits C received a settlement of around 200,000 punts as well as an unprecedented apology and admission of liability from the Irish state shortly before her death.
- Strong economic growth is producing at least 14,000 more jobs than predicted in the last budget, official figures showed.
- The Institute of Chartered Accountants in Ireland has decided to strengthen its disciplinary procedures by publishing the names of auditors which it strikes off its register.
- Life and pension policyholders with Norwich Union in Ireland stands to share in a windfall payout of at least 50 million as part of the demutualisation and flotation of the major UK insurer.
